claims.text: Controlled thermal annealing enhances chemical short-range order in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Controlled thermal annealing enhances surface segregation in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Enhanced chemical short-range order increases the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Surface segregation associated with enhanced short-range order increases nanoparticle thermal stability.
Enhanced short-range order delays the onset of surface premelting relative to a random solid solution.
Enhanced short-range order modifies the melting transition relative to a random solid solution.
Enhanced local chemical ordering promotes surface segregation.
Elements with lower electronegativity preferentially enrich the nanoparticle surface during annealing.
The altered local ordering and surface composition increase the energy barrier for surface premelting.
An increased energy barrier for surface premelting delays the observed premelting onset.
Annealed nanoparticles with enhanced short-range order will have a higher premelting-onset temperature than untreated randomly mixed nanoparticles.
Annealed nanoparticles with enhanced short-range order will exhibit a more gradual melting transition than untreated randomly mixed nanoparticles.
The proposed relationship should hold for sub-10 nm nanoparticles.
The proposed relationship should hold across equiatomic and near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Chemical short-range order can be characterized using diffraction or other local-ordering probes.
The comparison will use annealed particles and an untreated random-solid-solution control while holding nanoparticle size and atmosphere fixed.
